pointers.sentence: `django/utils/datastructures.py` holds the containers that the request, the ORM and the template engine share: `MultiValueDict`, the dictionary of lists under a request's query, form data and files; `CaseInsensitiveMapping`, under its headers; `ImmutableList`, `OrderedSet`, `DictWrapper` and `DeferredSubDict`.
Beside them, `make_hashable` in `django/utils/hashable.py` makes a value built of lists and dictionaries fit to be hashed.

A `MultiValueDict` is a `dict` whose stored values are lists, one to a key, with the methods that read and write a single value changed to hide the list (`django/utils/datastructures.py:MultiValueDict`).
`MultiValueDict._getlist` makes that copy when asked to, and otherwise returns the stored list itself (`django/utils/datastructures.py:MultiValueDict._getlist`).

Their comments say why: a subclass's `setlist` or `__setitem__` may store another value, and `QueryDict`'s do: they decode bytes, and its `setlist` stores a new list (`django/utils/datastructures.py:MultiValueDict.setlistdefault`, `django/http/request.py:QueryDict.setlist`).

Their comments say why: a subclass's `setlist` or `__setitem__` may store another value, and `QueryDict`'s do: they decode bytes, and its `setlist` stores a new list (`django/utils/datastructures.py:MultiValueDict.setlistdefault`, `django/http/request.py:QueryDict.setlist`).

Another `MultiValueDict` has its lists added to the ends of this one's; from a mapping, pairs or keyword arguments each value is appended to its key, so a plain dictionary whose value is a list appends the list as one value (`django/utils/datastructures.py:MultiValueDict.update`).

`MultiValueDict.copy` and `copy.copy` make a new dictionary with each list copied, their values shared; `copy.deepcopy` copies keys and lists deeply (`django/utils/datastructures.py:MultiValueDict.__copy__`, `django/utils/datastructures.py:MultiValueDict.__deepcopy__`).

`MultiValueDict.copy` and `copy.copy` make a new dictionary with each list copied, their values shared; `copy.deepcopy` copies keys and lists deeply (`django/utils/datastructures.py:MultiValueDict.__copy__`, `django/utils/datastructures.py:MultiValueDict.__deepcopy__`).

At protocols 2 to 5, the default among them, pickle writes a subclass of `dict` with the pairs its `items` yields, here the last values only, so `MultiValueDict.__getstate__` adds the whole lists to the state under `"_data"`, and `MultiValueDict.__setstate__` stores them again with `setlist` before restoring the rest of the instance's `__dict__` (`django/utils/datastructures.py:MultiValueDict.__setstate__`).

Uploaded files are kept in a plain one (`django/http/multipartparser.py:MultiPartParser._parse`), and the URL resolver files its candidates for reversing in one ([Reversing a name](../urls/reversing.md)) (`django/urls/resolvers.py:URLResolver._populate`).

`ImmutableList.complain`, which raises it, is bound to the name of every method by which a list changes, those behind item assignment, deletion, `+=` and `*=` included, except `list.clear`, which fails with Python's own message (`django/utils/datastructures.py:ImmutableList`).

A model's options hand out the lists of fields they cache as one, with a message that names the list and says to make a copy first ([The options: what a model keeps as `_meta`](../models/options.md)) (`django/db/models/options.py:make_immutable_fields_list`).

It keeps a dictionary from each key in lower case to the key as written and its value; a lookup lowers the key it is given, and iteration and `repr` give the keys as written (`django/utils/datastructures.py:CaseInsensitiveMapping`).

`OrderedSet` keeps its items as the keys of a dictionary made with `dict.fromkeys`, so membership is a dictionary lookup, and iteration, reversed or not, follows the order of insertion, which adding an item again does not change (`django/utils/datastructures.py:OrderedSet`).

Among the places Django uses it to drop duplicates and keep the order are the values on the right of an `In` lookup (`django/db/models/lookups.py:In.process_rhs`) and a model's ancestors (`django/db/models/options.py:Options.all_parents`).

`DictWrapper` is a dictionary that, for a key beginning with a given prefix, takes the prefix off and passes the value through a given function (`django/utils/datastructures.py:DictWrapper`).

The parameters of a model field's column type are one, over the field's `__dict__`, so that `"qn_column"` gives the column's name quoted ([Column types: from a field to a column](../backends/column-types.md)) (`django/db/models/fields/__init__.py:Field.db_type_parameters`).

`DeferredSubDict` looks a key up in a dictionary inside another only when indexed; its one user is the `{% partial %}` tag, whose partial may be defined below it ([Template partials: `{% partialdef %}` and `{% partial %}`](../templates/partials.md)) (`django/utils/datastructures.py:DeferredSubDict`, `django/template/defaulttags.py:partial_func`).

A dictionary becomes a tuple of its pairs sorted by key, each value made hashable in turn; a value that hashes is returned as it is, so a string or a frozenset is not taken apart; one that does not hash but can be iterated becomes a tuple of its items, each made hashable; anything else raises the `TypeError` of `hash` (`django/utils/hashable.py:make_hashable`).

Its users compare by value: `ValidationError.__hash__` ([Django's exceptions: `django.core.exceptions`](exceptions.md)); `Node.__hash__` (`django/utils/tree.py:Node.__hash__`); the identity of a `Q` object, a lookup and an expression ([Expressions: `resolve_expression` and `as_sql`](../sql/expressions.md)); the compiler, dropping a repeated ordering (`django/db/models/sql/compiler.py:SQLCompiler.get_order_by`); `Model._get_FIELD_display`, for a choice whose value is a list.
